page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 614 GB local SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage configurations.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics fall within the average range. Memory performance shows a distinct tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 1031.04 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths are weak, placing in the bottom 25% at 39.01 GB/sec and 22.73 GB/sec respectively.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads, database operations, and web serving. The inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD provides cost-efficient local storage capacity without requiring external disk attachments for temporary data. This configuration is suited for relational databases, static web serving, software compilation, and light language model inference tasks.
